findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous due to underscore separator
findings.body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` concatenates `name` and `parent` with underscores, but both values can themselves contain underscores. This means distinct (name, parent) pairs can produce identical cache keys. For example, name="a_b", parent="c" and name="a", parent="b_c" both yield the same key suffix "a_b_c". A denial cached for one resource/folder combination would incorrectly block access to the other. Consider using a separator that cannot appear in UIDs (e.g., a null byte or a structured encoding), or hashing the components separately.

findings.title: Denial cache can block access to a resource immediately after it is created
findings.body: The denial cache is checked before any other permission source. If a Check request for a specific resource is made before that resource exists (e.g., a pre-flight check, a shared link accessed before creation completes, or a retry from the UI), the denial is cached with a 30-second TTL. Once the resource is created and permissions are written to the DB, the user will still be denied for up to 30 seconds because the denial cache short-circuits before the permission cache or DB are consulted. This is the exact scenario the PR aims to fix (creator can't access newly created dashboard/folder), so the denial cache can reintroduce the bug under these timing conditions. Consider not caching denials for resources that don't yet exist, or checking the permission cache/DB before the denial cache when the denial entry is close to expiry.

findings.title: Every Check that misses the permission cache now hits the database
findings.body: When cached permissions exist but do not grant access to the requested resource, the code falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` which queries the database. In a scenario where a user has many permissions cached but repeatedly requests access to resources they don't have (e.g., probing different dashboard UIDs), each unique resource will trigger a full DB permission query before the denial cache is populated. The denial cache mitigates repeated requests for the same resource, but the first request per resource always hits the DB. For high-cardinality workloads this could increase DB load significantly compared to the previous behavior where a cached permission set was authoritative.

findings.title: List uses potentially stale cached permissions without DB fallback
findings.body: The `List` method uses `getCachedIdentityPermissions` and, on a cache hit, returns the cached permission set directly without falling through to the database. In contrast, `Check` now falls through to the DB when the cached permissions don't grant access. This asymmetry means a newly created dashboard might pass a `Check` (via DB fallback) but not appear in a `List` response until the permission cache expires. If the UI relies on `List` to populate navigation or search results, users may not see their newly created resources even though `Check` would allow access.
